recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If a future work group wants to revisit the historical choice to use targetElement/valueUri rather than a new focus-element/id extension, that work should be filed or reconciled against the FHIR Extension Pack rather than handled as a core-source fix for FHIR-27877.
issue_request: FHIR-27877 was Published/Persuasive and asked FHIR-I to define an extension, tentatively named focus-element, that lets a Reference or canonical identify specific element(s) within the referenced resource, with 0..* cardinality and rationale about being broader than Reference.reference URL fragments.
initial_application: The current solution was built on the already-approved FHIR-21284 targetElement and targetPath extensions. Core commit d4a3902f2ade29f77b3ec4495c012f01c6ad0c33 explicitly applied FHIR-27877 by changing targetElement and targetPath to Reference,canonical context in source/datatypes/reference-extensions-spreadsheet.xml and expanding targetElement's comment with the FHIR-27877 rationale. Earlier commit 38993a71efdea21922d51b0ba140af67cc084cec had introduced those extensions for Reference.
additional_context: A 2022-08-18 FHIR-I Zulip thread noted that FHIR-27877 ran into an existing extension, and participants identified targetElement/targetPath and Provenance usage as the likely solution. FHIR-I minutes from 2020-10-19 record the Persuasive 11-0-0 vote. Later commit dd468d4f1799dd79819315b211588ef1cf4586e0 intentionally removed extension definitions from the R5 core checkout; the authoritative targetElement and targetPath source now lives in /home/jmandel/work/fhir-extensions. FHIR-40918 later clarified the Extension Pack descriptions, while FHIR-39391 is already represented by a separate combined-branch audit commit.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No core source was changed because the core checkout no longer owns the extension definition and current active core source already links to the Extension Pack targetElement/targetPath definitions.
